# jnb


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

`jnb` runs the [J language](https://www.jsoftware.com/) in notebooks. It
provides `%%j` and `%j` magics for Python notebooks, and a Jupyter
kernel for notebooks written in J. Both load libj, J’s engine library,
into the Python process.

## Installation

Install J with `pip install jlanguage` or from
[jsoftware.com](https://www.jsoftware.com/). Then install jnb:

    pip install jnb

To register the magics automatically in IPython and Jupyter sessions,
run:

    jnb_install

You can also load them for one session with `%load_ext jnb`. The J
engine starts when you first run a magic.

## The `j` magics

`%%j` runs code and displays J’s output verbatim. `%j expr` returns an
expression’s value as Python data. The session keeps nouns and verbs
across cells:

``` python
%%j
m =: 3 3 $ i. 9
m +/ . * m
```

    15 18  21
    42 54  66
    69 90 111

``` python
z = %j m
z
```

    [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8]]

You can also use the [`J`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/jnb/j.html#j)
session class directly. It runs J code, transfers values in both
directions with `[]`, and converts J verbs to Python callables with
`fn`. See the [`j` module
documentation](https://answerdotai.github.io/jnb/j.html) for examples.

## The J Jupyter kernel

`jkernel` is a Jupyter kernel for J built on
[kernmini](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/kernmini). Register it with:

    python -m jnb.jkernel install

Use it from JupyterLab, nbclient,
[jupygate](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/jupygate), or agents using
clikernel. Workspace state persists across cells. A J attention
interrupt stops a computation without resetting the workspace.

The kernel runs `jnb/startup.ijs` from your XDG configuration directory
when that file exists. The default path is `~/.config/jnb/startup.ijs`.

## Limitations

- `%j` can return booleans, integers, floats and characters as Python
  data. Boxed, extended and rational values raise an error. Use `%%j` to
  display them.
- macOS and Linux are supported. The libj binding is untested on
  Windows, which is not yet supported.

## Learning J

Start with [Learning
J](https://www.jsoftware.com/help/learning/contents.htm) and the [J
wiki](https://code.jsoftware.com/wiki/), whose
[NuVoc](https://code.jsoftware.com/wiki/NuVoc) page is the reference for
every primitive.
